lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Orlando, this is Rachel. Is this an okay time to talk?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi, yes, perfect timing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Great. So today I'd like to hear how the walks after dinner went, check how you're feeling, and pick a goal for next week. Anything you want to add?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: No, that sounds good.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Any problems this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Honestly, rough week. I've been really tired.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're dealing with a lot, and you still made time for this call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Whatever you pick is fine with me. It's your plan.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Uh, I have to do something, I don't want the cancer back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's completely your call.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I want to get my energy back. Church on Sunday always throws me off.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Good for you for planning ahead.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: After dinner I can walk the dog, she needs it anyway.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You know your schedule better than anyone.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to walk after every dinner. That's the meal that matters most for your sugar.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Right.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Could someone in the family walk with you?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Good question.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: A short walk after dinner, even 10 minutes, really helps bring blood sugar down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What's worked for you before?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: If I plan it the night before, I can do it. My daughter keeps reminding me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: This is about more than the walks after dinner. It's about getting your life back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On one hand, the late dinners makes it really hard. On the other hand, you still want to make this work.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to be around and be well for the people you love.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, I want to get my energy back. I didn't think I'd like it, but I do.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to feel like yourself again.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So what would you like your goal to be for next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll try to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the late dinners gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll eat a bigger lunch so I'm not starving at night.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay, so your plan this week is to take a 10-minute walk after dinner on 3 days. Did I get that right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Tuesday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Orlando, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thanks, bye bye.

tags.note: Reports fatigue and a rough week
Desire to feel like herself again
Reason: wants to avoid cancer returning
Wants energy back; identifies Sunday church barrier
Plans to walk dog after dinner
Knows planning the night before works
Energy goal; now likes the walks

flags.reason: Directive 'You have to walk after every dinner' without permission; undermines autonomy.
'You have to make this a priority' pushes the participant; repeated directive pattern.
Grandkids motivation not explored or reflected; coach moved on to information.
Participant's own success strategy (planning night before) not reinforced or elaborated.

score.summary: Rachel built a clear, specific goal and a barrier backup plan, and summarized it accurately. However, she twice used directive 'have to' statements and did not reflect several change-talk moments, such as the grandkids motivation and the planning strategy.
strengths: Line 7 and 18: affirmed Orlando's effort and planning ahead.
Line 38 and 40: complex reflections captured ambivalence and his love for family.
Line 46 and 48: planned for barriers and checked the goal back accurately.
coaching_tips: Replace 'You have to' at line 21 and 28 with a question or permission-based offer, e.g., 'Would it help to talk about timing after dinner?'
Reflect the change talk at line 33 and 35 ('Your grandkids matter to you, and planning ahead works for you').
Check feelings and review last week's goal at the start rather than only asking about problems at line 5.
Ask about the good days (line 26) before offering information so he can draw on his own success.
